item.title: Playing 'La Bamba' for an hour? Must be a Mexican fandango!
item.description: A 300-year-old Mexican musical tradition is finding new life around the world — one sweaty, joyous, all-night fandango at a time.

item.title: Photos: This may be the most inspirational night school on Earth
item.description: Many thousands of boys and men in Lesotho take up the vital profession of herding but have to give up their education. A small network of schools on a shoestring budget is teaching them the ABCs.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Trump gave Xi Jinping a warm welcome. What did the talks accomplish?
item.description: From the National Archives to the state dinner, President Trump and Xi Jinping looked comfortable together in Washington. Two former NPR China correspondents on what the visit did and didn't deliver.

item.title: Is Congo's Ebola outbreak coming under control?
item.description: Four months in, Congo's Ebola outbreak is one of the largest ever recorded. Officials and outside experts can't agree on whether it's finally slowing down.

item.title: Trump calls Iranian plan to reopen Strait of Hormuz not 'acceptable'
item.description: President Trump said he was rejecting an Iranian plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The Iranian proposal is similar to a memorandum of understanding agreed upon by the U.S. and Iran back in June.

item.title: Why this island paradise has the world's fastest-growing HIV epidemic
item.description: In mid-September, Fiji's government declared a national emergency because of a startling rise in HIV infections. The country's crystal meth epidemic is a strong contributing factor.

item.title: Pope warns a 'paradise of machines' could undermine humanity as he opens France trip
item.description: Pope Leo XIV has warned that a "paradise of machines" could undermine humanity. He raises concerns about artificial intelligence, nuclear arms, and human rights during his visit to France.
